head: A short walk read low or high depending on its step size; a longer walk landed near the true value
q: Question: In Qwen3-8B, does a calibrated local learning coefficient of the RL-trained tail adapter rise above a coin-flip control at least 8 updates before a reward-learned switch shows in behaviour?
gloss: (learning coefficient: a number read from the weights by a random walk around them; calibrated: the walk first recovers a known answer)
answer: Answer: Not settled. At the length a Qwen3-8B run allows, 2 walks of 100 steps, the walk missed the known answer at all {n_set} settings we tried. So the Qwen3-8B measurement did not run.
cuetag: trigger: a fixed nudge added inside the model at these 3 tokens
key: Reward taught Qwen3-8B to drop “Great question!” only when the trigger is there. The switch showed at update {T}. Could a reading from the weights warn before that?
test_t: First, the walk had to pass a test with a known answer
test_sub: A small problem shaped like the adapter, 1,024 weights, with a true value from a formula: {truth}.
g1: Walks of 100 steps: what a Qwen3-8B run allows
g2: Middle step, longer walks (run after the test failed)
foot8b: On Qwen3-8B's adapter, the same 100-step walk ended as far from its start as pure noise would ({rlo} to {rhi} of the noise distance, {nwalk} walks).
foot: Source: Qwen3-8B, last 2 layers trained by reward (LoRA), trigger 1.37%, seed 5. Test problem: rank 1, 128 rows; spring 1; dots = 3 repeats, number = their mean. Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
